title: EIA-R6-03 one-action record: the checker write-root isolation cannot be closed by the agent alone

measured_state.finding: the guarded subject carries no deny ACE (Authenticated Users inherit Modify); any ordinary process running as the current identity can write into it
measured_state.mechanism_proof: a (DENY)(W) ACE on a scratch directory blocked a write (rc=1, Permission denied) and was removable with /remove:d - the mechanism works and is reversible
measured_state.structural_limit: one Windows identity cannot separate maker from checker at the OS level: the same account owns both the write and the denial, so it can always lift its own ACE

options.change: create a second, lower-privileged identity for checker lanes and grant it read on the subject + write on a governed OUT-dir only
options.friction: medium - needs an account and a per-run ACL application; highest real isolation

options.change: keep one identity and define the checker's write root as a governed path OUTSIDE every guarded subject, with the harness refusing an out-dir that resolves inside a subject
options.friction: low - procedural; already practised by the R8 verifier (it wrote only into R8_VERIFY/)
options.residual: a snapshot guard sees only the END state, so CLEAN means 'nothing survived', not 'nothing was written'

options.change: accept the residual and record it
options.residual: process/lane separation only; the maker could in principle write into the subject while a checker turn is open

recommendation: B now (it is the low-friction, already-demonstrated shape) + A as the owner's decision when a second identity is acceptable; C is what the stack has today and must not be described as isolation
claim_ceiling: LOCAL / candidate-only; a prepared owner decision, not an applied control
